generator.params.bud_area.note: The leaf area its `bud` look draws on an organ 1 m long (plantc's shading-area test), so it shades with what it shows: the bud is now its flower closed, where before it drew the fruit ovoid.

traits.height_typical_m.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944), Aquilegia formosa, Fig. 1775, p. 180: stems 5 dm to 10 dm high.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a graceful herb with blue-green, divided leaves and nodding red flowers with yellow centres and long spurs. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 0.6 m tall at 4 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: blue-green leaves; red and yellow flowers.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.note: The Flora of North America's account of the species, as SEINet's copy is quoted in search results (the page itself was not read): basal leaves 2 times ternately compound, 10 to 40 cm, much shorter than the stems; leaflets 14 to 68 mm, not crowded, the primary petiolules 16 to 95 mm.

appearance.organs.basal.shape.note: The basal leaves drawn twice ternate (spec rework P4): three divisions on long stalks, each of three leaflets, from its characters by the rules at the flowering plants; before, nine leaflets stood along a rachis. By eye: the divisions 160 degrees apart, the leaflets broad, fan-like and crenate (three teeth a side stand in for their lobes).

appearance.organs.leaf.shape.note: The stem leaves drawn once ternate, by eye: smaller and less divided than the basal ones, three leaflets from one point (spec rework P4).

traits.fruit_type.note: The Flora of North America's account of Aquilegia formosa, on the SEINet and NEON portals, as search results quote it (the page itself was not read): follicles 5 (the genus 5 to 10), against the achenes most of the buttercup family bear.

traits.spur_length_m.note: The Flora of North America's account of Aquilegia formosa, on the SEINet and NEON portals, as search results quote it (the page itself was not read): sepals red, 10 to 26 mm, held square to the flower's axis; petal blades yellow, 0 to 6 mm, each with a red spur 13 to 21 mm; stamens many, 12 to 17 mm; scalelike staminodes between the stamens and pistils; follicles 5 (the genus 5 to 10).

appearance.organs.flower.shape.note: Its flower laid out whorl by whorl (spec rework P5): five petals, each spurred, inside five red sepals, from the characters by the rules at the flowering plants. By hand, as the Flora of North America has them (as search results quote them; the pages themselves were not read): the sepals red and longer than the petal blades; the spurs about the flower's radius (the floras give the spur but not the flower's width); 40 stamens for its many.

appearance.organs.flower.form.note: The petal blades cupped round the stamens, the sepals spreading half as much, by eye from photographs.
